items.explain: Ana believed Priya was angry with her about the dropped baton. She saw Priya talking seriously and not smiling, and she was certain Priya was angry. It is at the end of the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Ana and Priya felt differently after the race. Which sentence is right?
options: Ana was embarrassed and worried, and Priya was calm and wanted to practice.
Ana was calm, and Priya was angry with Ana.
Ana and Priya were both angry with each other.
Ana was proud, and Priya was embarrassed and lonely.
items.hint: Find Ana's clues in the second paragraph. Then find what Priya said in the third paragraph.
items.explain: Ana was embarrassed and worried: she looked at her shoes and sat alone. Priya was calm: she was glad they finished and wanted to practice again. This is in the second and third paragraphs.

items.prompt: Ana's belief was wrong. Tap the sentence that tells why Priya was really talking to Ms. Ortiz.
items.hint: Ana could not hear Priya from across the field. Find what Priya says about it later.
items.explain: Priya was asking Ms. Ortiz about their handoff, because she thought she reached back too early. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: How did Ana feel at the very end of the story?
options: embarrassed
lonely
frustrated
relieved
items.hint: Find what Ana learned from Priya. Then look at what Ana's breath did.
items.explain: Ana felt relieved. Priya said she was not mad, and Ana let out a long breath and walked with her. It is the last sentence.

items.prompt: Priya said "Sure" when Maya asked if she was having fun. What did Priya want but not say?
options: to use the binoculars herself
to draw the birds in Maya's sketchbook
to count birds at a different creek
to get warm, and maybe go home
items.hint: Priya's word and her body do not match. Look at her hands, her feet, her teeth and where she kept looking.
items.explain: Priya wanted to get warm, and maybe go home. Her hands were deep in her pockets, she bounced on her toes, her teeth chattered and she kept glancing at the parking lot. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: At the start of the bird count, how were Maya's and Priya's feelings different?
options: Maya was cold and unhappy, and Priya was excited.
Maya was excited, and Priya was cold and unhappy.
Maya and Priya were both excited.
Maya was bored, and Priya was curious.
items.hint: Find what Maya did when she saw the chickadee. Then find three clues about Priya in the same paragraph.
items.explain: Maya was excited: she marked the chickadee with a big grin. Priya was cold and unhappy: her hands were in her pockets and her teeth chattered. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Sort the clues about Priya. Which show she was cold and unhappy, and which show she was curious and excited?

cards.text: Her hands were pushed deep into her pockets.
She shouted, "What was that?"
She kept glancing back toward the parking lot.
She watched the water for another kingfisher.
Her teeth were chattering.
She held the clipboard all morning.

items.hint: Ask if each clue came before or after the kingfisher dove into the creek.
items.explain: Before the kingfisher, Priya was cold and unhappy: hands in her pockets, glancing at the parking lot, teeth chattering. After it, she was curious and excited: she shouted a question, watched the water and kept the tally all morning.

items.prompt: Why did Maya ask Priya to be the tally keeper in the sunny spot?
options: Maya noticed Priya was cold and wanted to help her feel better.
Maya wanted to stand in the sunny spot herself.
Maya thought Priya was better at counting than at spotting birds.
Maya needed someone to watch the parking lot.
items.hint: Find what Maya looked at just before she asked. Think about why she gave Priya cocoa and a spot in the sun.
items.explain: Maya noticed Priya was cold and wanted to help her feel better. She looked at Priya's red nose and raised shoulders, gave her hot cocoa and sent her to the sunny spot. It is at the start of the third paragraph.

items.prompt: When Leo first saw the skeleton, what did he believe?
options: The bones in the hall were the real fossil bones.
The skeleton was a copy made from real fossils.
The skeleton came from a different kind of dinosaur.
Dr. Bell had built the skeleton by herself.
items.hint: Read what Leo whispered to Priya in the first paragraph.
items.explain: Leo believed the bones were the real fossil bones. He whispered, "I can't believe these are the actual bones." Dr. Bell then explained that it was a cast. It is at the end of the first paragraph.

items.prompt: How did Leo feel when he learned that the skeleton was a cast?
options: relieved
proud
disappointed
curious
items.hint: Look at Leo's smile, his feet, his voice and his hands at the end of the second paragraph.
items.explain: Leo felt disappointed. He stopped smiling, stepped back, said "So it's fake" in a flat voice and pushed his hands into his pockets. It is at the end of the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that shows Leo was amazed when he held the real tooth.
items.hint: Find the part after Dr. Bell handed Leo the gloves. Look at his breath and his hands.
items.explain: "Leo held his breath, and his hands stayed completely still" shows he was amazed. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Put Leo's feelings at the museum in the order they happened.
steps: Leo was excited by the giant skeleton.
Leo was disappointed to learn it was a copy.
Leo was amazed to hold a real tooth.
Leo was curious to learn more about dinosaurs.
items.hint: Read one paragraph at a time. For each one, ask what Leo did or said.
items.explain: First Leo walked around the skeleton three times. Then he stopped smiling when he heard it was a cast. In the lab he held his breath with the real tooth. On the bus home he asked Priya to quiz him on dinosaur facts.

items.prompt: Ben joked that the animals looked busy. How did he really feel?
options: proud
nervous
lonely
relieved
items.hint: A joke can hide a feeling. Look at where Ben stood, where his hands were and what his feet did when the crab came close.
items.explain: Ben felt nervous. He stood back with his hands behind his back, and when the crab came toward him he laughed but stepped back again. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Why did Maya tell Ben that the sea star moves very slowly?
options: She noticed Ben was nervous and wanted to help him feel safe.
She wanted Ben to leave the sea star alone.
She wanted to teach Ben a fact for a school report.
She thought Ben was bored and wanted to go home.
items.hint: Find what Maya noticed just before she spoke. Think about why a slow animal might help.
items.explain: Maya noticed Ben still had not touched a single animal, and she wanted to help him feel safe. A slow sea star is one he could watch the whole time. It is at the start of the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Sort the clues about Ben. Which show he was nervous, and which show he was curious?

cards.text: He stood back with his hands behind his back.
He touched the sea star twice more.
He made a joke about the animals being busy.
He asked the volunteer how sea stars eat.
He laughed loudly but took another step back.

items.hint: Ask if each clue came before or after Ben touched the sea star for the first time.
items.explain: Before he touched the sea star, Ben was nervous: he stood back, made a joke and stepped away from the crab. After, he was curious: he touched it again and asked how sea stars eat.

items.prompt: Before he touched it, what did Ben think the sea star would feel like?
options: rough and bumpy
sharp
warm
slimy
items.hint: Read what Ben said right after he touched it. Look for the words "I thought."
items.explain: Ben thought it would be slimy. He said, "I thought it would be slimy." Really it felt rough. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Before 7:42, what did Leo believe about Priya's time?
options: She had the exact minute right.
She was only guessing the time.
The station would come an hour later.
The station could not be seen from Harbor Town.
items.hint: Read what Leo asked Priya when he arrived, and what he said at 7:41.
items.explain: Leo believed Priya was only guessing. He said, "You're just guessing, right?" and at 7:41 he said, "See? Nothing." This is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: While they waited, how were Priya and Leo feeling differently?
options: Priya was calm and sure, and Leo did not think the station would come.
Priya was worried, and Leo was sure the station would come.
Priya and Leo were both nervous.
Priya was frustrated with Leo, and Leo was embarrassed.
items.hint: Find what Priya did while she waited. Then find what Leo did and said at 7:41.
items.explain: Priya was calm and sure: she checked her watch, pointed at the trees and waited calmly. Leo did not think it would come: he played with his popcorn and said, "See? Nothing." It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that shows Leo was amazed when he saw the station.
items.hint: Find what Leo was doing with his popcorn. Look at what happened to him when the light appeared.
items.explain: "Leo stopped moving, with a piece of popcorn halfway to his mouth" shows he was amazed. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: At the end of the story, what did Leo want?
options: to go home before it got cold
to see the space station pass over again
to eat the rest of his popcorn
to borrow Priya's watch
items.hint: Read the last sentence. Look at what Leo asked Priya.
items.explain: Leo wanted to see the space station again. He asked Priya when it would pass over again. It is the last sentence.

items.prompt: Maya said, "I'm just tired." How did she really feel?
options: nervous
frustrated
proud
lonely
items.hint: Her words say one thing. Look at her sleeping bag, her flashlight, her eyes and whether she closed them.
items.explain: Maya felt nervous. She zipped her bag to her chin, kept her flashlight on, looked quickly at every creak and did not close her eyes. These clues are in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Ben and Maya lay in the same dark hall. How did each of them feel when the lights went off?
options: Ben was nervous, and Maya was thrilled.
Ben and Maya were both tired and calm.
Ben was thrilled, and Maya was nervous.
Ben was disappointed, and Maya was curious.
items.hint: Find what Ben whispered. Then find what Maya did with her sleeping bag and flashlight.
items.explain: Ben was thrilled: he whispered that it was the best night of his life. Maya was nervous: she zipped her bag to her chin and kept her flashlight on. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: What helped Maya stop feeling nervous?
options: Ben told her that the museum was safe.
The staff turned the main lights back on.
She fell asleep and forgot about the shadows.
Dr. Bell's lantern tour helped her get to know every skeleton.
items.hint: Find what happened in the third paragraph. Then read what Maya told Ben at the end.
items.explain: Dr. Bell's lantern tour helped Maya get to know every skeleton. She sketched each one, and at the end she said, "I know every one of them now." This is in the third and last paragraphs.

items.prompt: Put Maya's feelings in the order they happened.
steps: Maya was nervous about the shadows in the dark hall.
Maya was unsure, but she followed the lantern tour.
Maya grew calmer as she sketched each skeleton.
Maya felt safe enough to switch off her flashlight.
items.hint: Follow Maya's flashlight and her drawing hand from the second paragraph to the end.
items.explain: First Maya kept her flashlight on and watched every creak. Then she slowly unzipped her bag to join the tour. Her drawing hand grew steadier as she sketched. At the end she switched off her flashlight without being asked.

items.prompt: How did Sam feel when he found the empty egg carton?
options: embarrassed
relieved
lonely
frustrated
items.hint: Look at what Sam did with the carton and his hands, and how he spoke.
items.explain: Sam felt frustrated. He slammed the carton shut, pressed his hands flat on the counter and said that the plan was ruined with his teeth pressed together. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: What helped Sam feel settled again after he found the empty carton?
options: His dad drove to another town to buy eggs.
He decided to buy a cake when the store opened at noon.
Grandma Rose brought him eggs from the bakery.
He took slow breaths and remembered a cake recipe that needs no eggs.
items.hint: Read the third paragraph. Find what Sam did at the window, and what he remembered next.
items.explain: Sam counted ten slow breaths and remembered an old cookbook with a chocolate cake made without eggs. Then he wrote the new steps on his card. It is in the third paragraph.

options: The bakery had no eggs that day.
He did not want to spoil the surprise.
He was upset with Grandma Rose.
His dad told him not to call her.
items.hint: Remember what Sam wanted to do for Grandma Rose. Then read the last sentence of the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Before he saw Priya's pencil mark, what did Sam believe?
options: The song was going perfectly.
Priya wanted to play the song faster.
Priya did not like the folk song.
Ms. Gray wanted them to choose another song.
items.hint: Find what Sam said after each practice. Then read the first sentence of the third paragraph.
items.explain: Sam believed the song was going perfectly. He said "That was our best one yet!" because Priya never said that anything was wrong. This is in the second and third paragraphs.

items.prompt: What did Priya want but not say for two weeks?
options: to choose a different song
to stop playing at the music night
to play the middle section more slowly
to play the guitar part herself
items.hint: Look at her pencil mark and at what she admitted in the third paragraph.
items.explain: Priya wanted to play the middle section more slowly. She marked it "SLOWER" and later admitted she had wanted to ask Sam to slow down for two weeks. This is in the second and third paragraphs.

items.prompt: Sort the clues. Which show Priya was unhappy with the speed, and which show Sam was happy with it?

She packed up faster than usual.
He grinned after every practice.

items.hint: First decide who each clue is about. Then ask what that person felt about the speed.
items.explain: Priya frowned, played scratchy notes and packed up quickly, so she was unhappy with the speed. Sam tapped his foot, grinned and called it their best one, so he was happy with it. They felt differently about the same practices.

items.prompt: Priya said "Yeah, good" after every practice. Why did she keep her wish a secret for two weeks?
options: She wanted Sam to play even faster.
She worried that Sam would think she was not good enough.
She thought the music night was canceled.
She did not want to play with Sam at all.
items.hint: Read what Priya admitted after Sam asked his question.
items.explain: Priya worried that Sam would think she was not good enough. She admitted this in the third paragraph, after Sam asked if the middle part was too fast.

items.prompt: How did Ben feel when he saw "Time remaining: 8 hours"?
options: relieved
frustrated
proud
curious
items.hint: Look at the sound Ben made, how he sat down and what he kept doing.
items.explain: Ben felt frustrated. He groaned, dropped onto the couch, kept checking the bar and sat down harder each time. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Ben and Leo saw the same slow download. How did each of them react?
options: Ben stayed calm, and Leo was frustrated.
Ben and Leo were both frustrated.
Ben and Leo were both excited.
Ben was frustrated, and Leo stayed calm.
items.hint: Find what Ben did on the couch. Then find what Leo said and did.
items.explain: Ben was frustrated: he groaned and kept checking the bar. Leo stayed calm: he shrugged, said "It will finish when it finishes" and went for juice. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Fill in the story map about Ben's Saturday.

slots.label: What Ben wanted
options: to play a railroad board game
to play the new racing game at ten o'clock
to eat pretzels with Leo
to finish his longest route

options: Leo forgot to buy the game.

options: happy and busy with the board game
still frustrated
lonely

items.hint: Do one box at a time. The want is in the first paragraph, the problem in the second, what he did instead in the third, and the ending in the last.
items.explain: Ben wanted to play the new racing game at ten. The download would take eight hours. He played a railroad board game with Leo's little brother instead. At the end he was so happy with it that he asked to finish the round first.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that shows Ben's feelings had changed by the end.
items.hint: Find the moment the download finished. Look at what Ben did and said then.
items.explain: "Can we finish this round first?" shows Ben's feelings had changed. The game he waited all day for was ready, but he wanted to keep playing the board game. Ben not moving from the floor shows it too. It is in the last paragraph.

items.prompt: Why did Priya leave the boy alone during the workshop?
options: She believed he thought robots were boring.
She knew he was worried that he would break the parts.
Mrs. Hall asked her to help only the other children.
He told her he already knew how to build robots.
items.hint: Find what Priya decided after the boy shook his head. Be careful: what Priya knew then is different from what was true.
items.explain: Priya believed he thought robots were boring. She decided this after he shook his head and looked out the window. She learned the truth only later, from Mrs. Hall. It is at the end of the second paragraph.

items.prompt: How did the boy really feel at the start of the workshop?
options: bored
proud
nervous
lonely
items.hint: What Priya guessed was wrong. Read what the boy did at the racing table, and what Mrs. Hall learned.
items.explain: The boy felt nervous. He loved robots but was worried he would break the parts, so he reached for a wheel and quickly pulled his hand back. This is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that shows the boy wanted to touch the robots but felt unsure.
items.hint: Look in the third paragraph for something the boy started to do and then stopped.
items.explain: "He reached out to touch one of the wheels, then quickly pulled his hand back" shows he wanted to touch it but felt unsure. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: How did Priya feel when she learned the truth, and what did she do next?
options: She felt frustrated, and she asked Mrs. Hall to help him.
She felt lonely, and she packed up the spare kit.
She felt proud, and she raced the finished robots.
She felt a little embarrassed, and she sat down to help the boy build.
items.hint: Look at Priya's cheeks at the start of the last paragraph. Then read what she did with the spare kit.
items.explain: Priya felt a little embarrassed, because her cheeks felt warm when she learned she had guessed wrong. Then she opened a spare kit and sat down to help the boy. It is in the last paragraph.

items.prompt: When the boat first tipped, how did Ana and Leo each feel?
options: Leo was nervous, and Ana was thrilled.
Leo and Ana were both calm.
Leo was embarrassed, and Ana was frustrated.
Leo was thrilled, and Ana was nervous.
items.hint: In the second paragraph, find what Leo did when the boat tipped. Then find what Ana's hands and voice did.
items.explain: Leo was thrilled: he whooped, leaned out and laughed. Ana was nervous: she gripped the bench until her knuckles turned pale and asked her question in a small voice. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Which clue shows Ana's feeling through her body?
options: She asked, "Is it supposed to lean like this?"
Her knuckles turned pale as she grabbed the bench.
Leo whooped and leaned out over the side.
The instructor had been sailing for thirty years.
items.hint: Check who each option is about. Then ask: is this something Ana said, or something her body did?
items.explain: Her pale knuckles as she grabbed the bench are a body clue. Her question is a word clue, and the other two options are about Leo and the instructor. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: What helped Ana go from nervous to confident?
options: She learned why the boat leans and how to control it with the rope.
Leo held the rope for her the whole time.
The wind stopped, so the boat no longer leaned.
The instructor steered the boat back to the dock early.
items.hint: Read the third paragraph. Find what the instructor explained and what she handed to Ana.
items.explain: Ana learned why the boat leans and how to control it with the rope. The instructor explained the keel, and Ana practiced letting the rope out and pulling it in until her shoulders relaxed. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Put Ana's feelings in the order they happened.
steps: Ana was nervous when the boat tipped.
Ana grew calmer as she learned to use the rope.
Ana felt confident and wanted to go faster.
Ana was proud to teach Leo the rope trick.
items.hint: Follow Ana from the second paragraph to the last. Look at her hands, her shoulders and what she asked for.
items.explain: First Ana gripped the bench. Then her shoulders slowly relaxed as she used the rope. Next she asked to go faster. Last, she taught Leo the trick and grinned the whole way in.

items.prompt: How did Ben feel when Ana was chosen as captain?
options: relieved that he did not have to be captain
proud of Ana and disappointed for himself
upset with Ana and the whole team
embarrassed and lonely
items.hint: Remember what Ben had hoped for. Then find clues from the field and different clues from the walk home.
items.explain: Ben felt proud of Ana and disappointed for himself. He hugged her first and meant it when he said she would be great, but he had hoped to be captain, and he kicked a pebble for three blocks. This is in the first two paragraphs.

items.prompt: How did Ana feel on the walk home after the vote?
options: proud and completely calm
annoyed with Ben for being so quiet
excited to be captain and worried about Ben
disappointed that she was chosen
items.hint: Read the start of the third paragraph. Find one clue about being captain and one clue about her brother.
items.explain: Ana was excited to be captain and worried about Ben. She noticed he was quiet, kept glancing at him and her smile kept fading. It is at the start of the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Sort Ben's clues. Which show he was proud of Ana, and which show he was disappointed?

cards.text: He was the first one to hug his sister.
He kicked a pebble for three entire blocks.
He told her, "You'll be great at it."
He answered Ana's questions with single words.
He clapped when the votes were counted.

items.hint: A person can feel two things at once. Ask if each clue is about Ana's success or about Ben's own hope.
items.explain: Hugging Ana first, clapping and saying she would be great show Ben was proud of her. Kicking a pebble for three blocks and answering with single words show he was disappointed for himself.

items.prompt: Why did Ana ask Ben to lead the warm-ups?
options: Coach Novak told her that Ben had to lead them.
She did not want to be captain anymore.
She wanted to stretch in the back row.
She noticed he was disappointed and gave him a job he was good at.
items.hint: Find what Ana noticed about her brother. Then read the reason she gave him.
items.explain: Ana noticed Ben was disappointed and gave him a job he was good at. She saw how quiet he was, and she said a good captain chooses the best person for each responsibility. It is in the third paragraph.

items.prompt: Leo told the ranger it was fine to work alone. How did he really feel?
options: proud
lonely
relieved
curious
items.hint: Do not stop at what Leo told the ranger. Look at where he walked, where he ate and what he told his mom.
items.explain: Leo felt lonely. He hiked at the back, ate apart from the others, was left without a partner and told his mom he did not want to go back. It is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: What did Leo want but not say at camp?
options: to be friends with the kids in his group
to work alone on every challenge
to go home early every day
to walk at the front of the line
items.hint: Think about why Leo told a joke on the first morning. Then compare what he told the ranger with what he told his mom.
items.explain: Leo wanted to be friends with the kids in his group. He tried a joke on the first day, and he felt so alone that he did not want to go back. Saying he liked working alone hid what he wanted. This is in the first and second paragraphs.

items.prompt: What changed how Leo felt about camp?
options: The ranger told two kids to be his partners.
His friends came back early and joined the camp.
He shared his idea for the bridge, and his team saw how helpful it was.
He told a funnier joke on Wednesday morning.
items.hint: Read the third and fourth paragraphs. Find what Leo showed his team, and what happened after the bridge held.
items.explain: Leo shared his idea for the bridge, and his team saw how helpful it was. The X made the bridge hold, the girl told everyone it was his idea, and two kids sat with him at lunch. This is in the third and last paragraphs.

items.prompt: Tap the sentence that shows Leo was now happy to go back to camp.
items.hint: Compare the end of the second paragraph with the end of the story. Look at what Leo did that evening.
items.explain: "That evening, Leo packed his bag for Thursday before his mom even asked" shows he was happy to go back. On Tuesday evening he had said he did not want to go. It is the last sentence.

items.prompt: How did Sam feel when he saw the final version of the map?
options: proud and completely satisfied
proud that it won, but disappointed about the gray line
relieved that the work was finished
embarrassed that the designer had changed his streets
items.hint: Remember how Sam felt when he heard he had won. Then look at what he did after he saw the gray line.
items.explain: Sam was proud that his map won, but disappointed about the gray line. He ran around the yard when he heard the news, but after he saw the final version he stared, closed the laptop and stayed in his room. This is in the second paragraph.

items.prompt: Sam said, "It looks very professional." What did he really want?
options: to make all the streets lighter
to hang the map in his own room
to draw a new map for next year
to have the railway line changed back to red
items.hint: Remember why Sam made the railway red in the first paragraph. Then read what he finally told his dad.
items.explain: Sam wanted the railway line changed back to red. He made it red so visitors could find the station, and at dinner he said the red line was the most important part. This is in the first and third paragraphs.

items.prompt: Why did Sam wait before he asked the designer to change the line?
options: He did not notice the gray line at first.
His dad told him not to send a message.
He liked the gray line better than the red one.
He worried she would think he was ungrateful.
items.hint: Read what Sam explained to his dad at dinner.
items.explain: Sam worried that the designer would think he was ungrateful. He said this at dinner, in the third paragraph.

steps.say: The question asks how Maya felt when she stood at the front. I find that part.
The next sentence says her hands shook as she held the paper.
Then she read the first page very quietly.
Shaking hands and a quiet voice can show that a person is nervous.
